newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse trade at record close.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse trade at record close.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended floor trade on Friday at a new record close, supported by strength on other bourses, the firm dollar and data showing improved domestic business confidence.
The expiry of certain options contracts on the DAX also helped push the market upwards, dealers said.
The DAX index closed bourse trade up 18.56 points, or 0.68 percent, at 2,734.20, slightly off the day's high of 2,739.26.
The market has been consolidating since the last record DAX high of 2,728.64 was reached on Tuesday.

Dealers said some players had gone short in late floor trading on Thursday on fears over Russian political instability and were hurrying back into the market. "The Russian situation isn't as bad as we thought," said one dealer.
The September West German IFO business climate index rose to 95.7 from 94.4, reflecting an improvement in business confidence.
Among individual shares, car maker Daimler Benz continued to be a favourite and closed bourse trade up 1.35 marks, or 1.5 percent, at 89.80 marks.
Mercedes-Benz, part of the Daimler group, said sales for commercial vehicles had risen five percent to 248,600 vehicles for the first nine months of 1996.

Shares in Europe's leading insurer, Allianz AG Holding, gained almost two percent to end bourse dealings up 45 marks at 2727 marks, after the firm said it expects a decision by German and European cartel authorities by November over its plans to take over Vereinte Holding AG insurance group.
Sportsware firm Adidas dropped over five percent or 7.80 marks to 135 marks in floor trade. "There are rumours that earnings downgrades are in the pipeline," said one trader.
Dealers said the stock, which had risen after it said it would be a main sponsor of the 1998 soccer World Cup, was not being seen as positively as before by banks.
New stock dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care added over almost seven percent in floor trade, rising 8.60 marks to 132.10, after the group's shares gained ground in New York.
